newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-BAERGA DELIVERS WIN FOR METS OVER BRAVES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-BAERGA DELIVERS WIN FOR METS OVER BRAVES.

text.p: Carlos Baerga delivered two big hits on Tuesday as the surprising, surging New York Mets beat the defending National League champion Atlanta Braves for the second night in a row for their sixth consecutive victory.

Baerga tied the game at 5-5 with a two-run homer in the eighth and won it with an RBI single in the bottom of the ninth as the Mets closed to within four games of the first-placed Braves in the NL East with a dramatic 6-5 win.
RBI singles by Jeff Blauser and Chipper Jones in the seventh put the Braves ahead 5-3 before Baerga took over.
Carl Everett doubled to left field off Braves reliever Mike Bielecki and Baerga, batting left-handed, followed by lofting a 1-0 pitch just over the wall in the left-field corner to tie the game.

In the ninth, Braves closer Mark Wohlers (2-3) walked Todd Hundley with one out before Everett singled sharply to right field to put runners on the corners. Baerga then lined a 1-2 pitch over the head of drawn-in shortstop Jeff Blauser to score Hundley with the game-winner.
"I haven't really hit the ball well against him," Baerga said of Wohlers. "With two strikes I was just trying to make contact. It is really exciting, this was my night."

Greg McMichael (4-6) escaped a bases-loaded jam in the top of the ninth to notch the victory as New York moved 11 games over .500. Wohlers, who entered a tie game in the eighth, gave up two hits and a walk, retiring just two batters.
"Things sure are not going our way, I'll tell you that," Braves manager Bobby Cox said. "If you blow one eighth-inning lead, that's one too many."
In Montreal, Lenny Harris's one-out single in the top of the 10th inning drove home Eduardo Perez with the winning run as the Cincinnati Reds edged the Expos 7-6.
Harris blooped the first pitch he saw from Dave Veres (2-2) into right field, easily scoring Perez, who had four hits in the game, including a home run, and three RBIs.
The Reds overcame a 5-4 deficit in the ninth, taking the lead on Curtis Goodwin's two run single.
Reds closer Jeff Shaw (2-0) notched the win despite allowing a game-tying homer by Mike Lansing in the bottom of the ninth inning that sent the game into extra innings.
In San Francisco, Shawn Estes allowed one run and seven hits to become the third 10-game winner in the National League as the Giants beat the San Diego Padres 4-1.
Estes (10-2) walked two and struck out six in eight innings before giving way to Rod Beck, who pitched a 1-2-3 ninth for his league-leading 25th save in 27 opportunities.
Darryl Hamilton and Jose Vizcaino had RBI singles in a three-run second inning and Bonds hit his 17th homer in the third for the Giants.
Nine of Bonds's last 18 hits have been homers, all in the last 16 games.
In Philadelphia, Al Leiter, Jay Powell and Robb Nen combined on a six-hitter to lead the Florida Marlins to a 4-1 victory over the Phillies.
Leiter (6-5) allowed a run and four hits over six innings for the win and Nen notched his 20th save.

Scott Ruffcorn (0-2), who had trouble finding the plate in 4 1/3 innings, suffered the loss. He gave up two runs and two hits but walked an astounding 10 batters, including Kurt Abbott and Edgar Renteria who walked and scored in the third.
Jim Eisenreich and Jeff Conine had RBI doubles for Florida.

In Houston, Jon Lieber allowed just an unearned run and three hits over seven innings and Al Martin and Kevin Young each homered and drove in two runs as the Pittsburgh Pirates defeated the Astros 8-3.
Lieber (4-8) allowed a double and two singles before Marc Wilkins gave up a pair of runs in relief. Clint Sodowsky tossed a scoreless ninth to preserve the victory.

Martin, who was activated off the disabled list just prior to the game, hit a two-run homer in the first to stake the Pirates to a 2-0 lead. Young added a solo shot later in the inning and drove in another run in a three-run seventh.
In St Louis, Andy Benes allowed one run over seven innings and Ron Gant had three hits and drove in three runs to lead the Cardinals to a 7-2 victory over the Chicago Cubs.
Delino DeShields singled, doubled, tripled and scored three times for the Cardinals, who have won three of their last four games following a five-game losing streak.

Benes (6-3) allowed four hits, walked two and struck out seven for the victory. Terry Mulholland (5-8) was reached for five runs and seven hits in 3 1/3 innings to suffer his fourth consecutive defeat.
In Los Angeles, Larry Walker hit a two-run homer and Ellis Burks had a pair of RBI doubles to lead the Colorado Rockies to a 6-2 victory over the Dodgers.
Walker belted his 22nd home run off Los Angeles starter Pedro Astacio (3-7) and Burks doubled home Andres Galarraga in the first inning to stake Colorado to a 3-0 lead.
In the third, Burks doubled in Walker and scored on Dante Bichette's RBI single for a 5-1 lead.
Darren Holmes (3-1) gave up two runs on five hits in eight innings with seven strikeouts to pick up the win for Colorado.
